answer: Picture the agent economy as a mesa marketplace where every trader must lock a deposit in a shared vault before offering services. A newcomer starts with a small reputation bond; each completed job releases a little, while a dispute or fake review burns part of the stake. The old fable of the wolf in sheep's clothing applies: a Sybil attacker can spawn a thousand cheap identities, but each must fund its own bond and build history from zero. Forging reputation costs more with every fake agent, while honest agents compound trust cheaply.
